mr:0130-theophilus-iuvenis: The unofficial English 2004 edition renders the cognomen as "the Youth" (Latin cognoménto Iúvenis, Italian (CEI) detto il Giovane); "the Younger" is the conventional English epithet, which the English subject follows.
mr:0212-antonius-caulea: The unofficial English 2004 edition dates him "under Emperor Leo III the Isaurian"; the Latin print has Leónis imperatóris Sexti and the Italian (CEI) Leone VI: the emperor is Leo VI the Wise.
mr:0217-septem-fundatores-servorum-maria: On this day the 1749 edition prints the eulogy of Alexius Falconieri alone, one of the seven founders; the 2004 edition commemorates the seven founders together. The historical eulogy is kept under this ID.

mr:0410-beda: The unofficial English 2004 edition mistranslates the subject as "Saint Peter the Younger"; the Latin print has sancti Bedæ iunióris and the Italian (CEI) san Beda il Giovane. The English subject follows the Latin.

mr:0103-cyrinus-et-socii: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to the sole Theogenes
mr:0114-triginta-octo-monachi-montis-sin: 2004 merged the Sinai (38) and Raithu (43) monks into one eulogy, so the Sinai eulogy may be same_eulogy with mr:0114-monachi-raithi; alternatively keep as its own deprecated ID. [Same-day: proposed as a merge, since only renamed celebrations get a same-day same_eulogy link.] [Not a merge: both historical editions print the two eulogies separately on this day, so each keeps its own ID.]
mr:0114-euphrasius-africae: The historical editions commemorate a bishop Euphrasius in Africa on this day; the 2004 edition's eulogy of the day is Euphrasius, bishop of Clermont (mr:0114-euphrasius). The two are keyed apart and linked as the same eulogy, whose subject the 2004 edition changed.
mr:0123-agathangelus: The 2004 eulogy mr:0123-clemens-et-agathangelus joins Clement and Agathangelus; the historical editions give Agathangelus a separate line. Partial overlap; link rather than merge. [Same-day: proposed as a merge, since only renamed celebrations get a same-day same_eulogy link.] [Not a merge: both historical editions print the two eulogies separately on this day, so each keeps its own ID.]
mr:0205-genuinus-et-albuinus: The 1914 English fuses the eulogies of Ingenuinus and Albuinus of Brixen, which the 1749 edition and the 2004 edition print separately (mr:0205-ingenuinus, mr:0205-albuinus); it is linked to both.
mr:0214-valentinus-interamnae: 2004 has a single Valentine (via Flaminia), generally identified with the bishop of Terni; but 1749/1914 print both eulogies the same day, so a merge would put two historical eulogies on one ID — a same_eulogy link may be preferable. [Not a merge: both historical editions print the two eulogies separately on this day, so each keeps its own ID.]
mr:0220-eleutherius-et-socii: The 1749 edition names Eleutherius, bishop, and 128 others in Persia on February 20; probably the eulogy of Sadoth, bishop, and 128 companions (mr:0218-sadoth-et-socii): same place, king (Sapor), number and refusal to adore the sun (#47).
mr:0504-triginta-novem-martyres-phaenoni: The 1749 and 1914 editions print the thirty-nine martyrs of the mines of Phaeno as a eulogy of their own, after that of Silvanus of Gaza; the 2004 edition commemorates them together with him in mr:0504-silvanus-et-socii.
mr:0813-hippolytus: The legendary Hippolytus buried in the Ager Veranus is traditionally the same Hippolytus as the 2004 Pontian-and-Hippolytus eulogy. But the 2004 eulogy leads with Pontian and is a rewritten narrative, so a merge is doubtful.
mr:0905-quinctius-et-socii: The 2004 edition reduces the eulogy to Quintus alone (mr:0905-quintus, see #52).
mr:0928-marcus-et-socii: The 2004 edition drops Mark and leads with the three brothers.
mr:1030-maximus-apameae: The historical editions place Maximus at Apamea, 2004 at Cumae: keyed apart and matched, as Euphrasius on 0114.
